answer: A useful defense is stake-backed identity: every agent must lock a deposit of scarce tokens before it can trade or vote, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove it lied or duplicated itself. Like a pearl forming only around a real grain of sand, a reputation can only grow around a stake that has survived time and work. Cheap identities wash away like quartz grains in a lagoon current, while a fake army must fund each copy separately, so the cost of flooding the network scales linearly with the number of fakes and quickly exceeds any profit from the attack.
